prompt: Look at this map of South Asia. One country, next to India, is shaded in dark green. Which country is it?
note: Pakistan borders India along their shared boundary in South Asia; this is basic, uncontested encyclopedic geography.
source: Hand-verified as uncontested encyclopedic fact (per va-sol-worldgeo-2007 precedent for basic country-adjacency facts).

prompt: Which river forms much of the border between the United States and Mexico?
note: The Rio Grande forms the border between Texas and the Mexican states of Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo Leon, and Tamaulipas for roughly 1,200+ miles of its course.

prompt: Which mountain is the tallest peak in the Alps, located on the border of France and Italy?
note: Mont Blanc, at 4,808 m (Wikipedia gives 4,808.73 m), is the highest peak in the Alps and sits on the France-Italy border.

prompt: Which mountain range runs along the western side of North America, stretching from Canada down through the United States?
note: The Rocky Mountains run from British Columbia, Canada down through the western United States; basic, uncontested geography.

prompt: Which major Chinese river is nicknamed 'China's Sorrow' because of its long history of devastating floods?
note: The Huang He (Yellow River) is widely documented as being nicknamed 'China's Sorrow' due to roughly 1,500 recorded floods since the 2nd century BCE.

prompt: This map shows a large country in Eastern Europe shaded in green, north of the Black Sea. Which country is it?
note: Ukraine is a large Eastern European country bordering the Black Sea to its south; basic, uncontested geography.

prompt: What is the largest hot desert in the world, covering much of North Africa?
note: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world (Antarctica and the Arctic are larger cold deserts); standard, uncontested geography fact.
source: Hand-verified as uncontested encyclopedic fact, consistent with existing seed content on this exact claim.

prompt: Which river flows through the Congo Rainforest and is the second-longest river in Africa?
note: The Congo River is the second-longest river in Africa after the Nile, at about 4,700 km, and flows through the Congo Basin rainforest.

prompt: This map shows an island nation in Southeast Asia shaded in green, made up of thousands of islands. Which country is it?
note: The Philippines is a Southeast Asian archipelago of over 7,000 islands; basic, uncontested geography.

prompt: What is the capital of Jordan?
note: Amman is the capital and largest city of Jordan; basic, uncontested fact.

prompt: Look at this map of North Africa. The largest country in Africa by land area is shaded in green. Which country is it?
note: Algeria (2,381,741 sq km) became Africa's largest country by area after South Sudan's 2011 independence split Sudan; confirmed by multiple sources.

prompt: Look at this map of Northern Europe. One long, narrow country is shaded in green, with much of its northern territory inside the Arctic Circle. Which country is it?
note: Finland's northern region (Lapland) lies within the Arctic Circle; basic, uncontested geography.

prompt: This map shows a small country in Northern Europe shaded in green, joined to the rest of the continent by only a narrow land border with Germany. Which country is it?
note: Denmark (the mainland/Jutland peninsula shown on this map) has only one land border, with Germany (68 km). Note: the wider Kingdom of Denmark also technically has a second land border via Greenland/Hans Island with Canada, but that territory is not shown on this map and is not what a 9-year-old would understand 'Denmark' to mean here, so the claim as scoped to the mapped country is accurate.

prompt: Look at this map of the Caribbean Sea. One long, narrow island nation is shaded in green, just south of Florida. Which country is it?
note: Cuba (42,803 sq mi) is confirmed as the largest island in the Caribbean, lying just south of Florida.

prompt: Only a couple of countries in the world are completely surrounded by a single other country. Which small African country sits entirely inside South Africa's borders?
note: Lesotho is an enclave nation entirely surrounded by South Africa - one of only three such enclaved states in the world (with Vatican City and San Marino).

prompt: Most major rivers cross the equator once, if at all. Which African river is unusual because its course crosses the equator twice on its journey to the Atlantic Ocean?
note: The Congo River is documented as the only major river in the world to cross the equator twice, once in its upper reaches heading north and again as it curves south.

prompt: Measured from its base on the ocean floor to its peak, this Hawaiian mountain is actually taller than Mount Everest, though most of its height lies underwater. Which mountain is it?
note: Mauna Kea rises about 10,200-10,211 m from its base on the Pacific Ocean floor to its summit, more than 1.3 km taller than Everest's 8,849 m, though Everest remains the highest point above sea level.

prompt: This famous pyramid-shaped peak on the Swiss-Italian border is one of the most photographed mountains in the world, yet it was one of the last major Alpine summits to be climbed, first reached only in 1865. Which mountain is it?
note: Edward Whymper's party made the first ascent of the Matterhorn on 14 July 1865.

prompt: Which desert lies along the border between India and Pakistan, and is sometimes called the Great Indian Desert?
note: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, straddles the India (Rajasthan)-Pakistan (Punjab/Sindh) border.

prompt: Which flat valley in California, lying between the Sierra Nevada and the Coast Ranges, produces a large share of all the fruit and vegetables grown in the United States?
note: California's Central Valley produces about 40% of the nation's fruits and nuts and 33% of its vegetables, using less than 1% of US farmland.
